```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(datagenerator)
```

Synthetic data is useful for teaching, testing pipelines, and simulation. It is
also easy to mistake for real data. This vignette lists what to watch for.

## Synthetic is not the same as anonymous

Data generated from parameters you chose has no link to real people. Data
generated from parameters **estimated from real records** can leak information
about those records. Stage 2 of this package (fitting to real data) will warn
before estimating anything from real records. Stage 1 generators only use
parameters you type in.

## Synthetic data can carry bias

The parameters you choose encode assumptions about a population. A mean income
of 50 or a 60/30/10 split of categories is a claim about the world. Defaults in
this package are deliberately neutral and do not encode real-population
assumptions. Check any parameters you borrow from a source.

## The label stays on the data

Every dataset prints a banner and carries a provenance record:

```{r label}
x <- gen_numeric(3, mean = 100, sd = 15, seed = 1)
x
dg_meta(x)$synthetic
```

Keep the label when you save, share, or combine data. The label can be lost
by some operations (for example, many `dplyr` verbs return plain tibbles), so
recheck with `dg_meta()` before you rely on it.

## Do not use this package to fabricate evidence

Do not generate records, receipts, results, or survey responses and present
them as observed. Do not use synthetic data to support a research claim unless
the synthetic nature and its assumptions are stated openly. Synthetic data is a
tool for testing methods and teaching, not a source of evidence.
